name: Kelden AdaptFlex Variable-Geometry Trouser
description: Slim-cut trousers in matte black synth-wool blend with memory-fiber panels at the thigh, knee, and calf that expand and contract to accommodate variable-geometry augmented limbs — legs that shift configuration between modes. The waistband and hip are cut generously, with internal adjustment cords. They look like a clean, professional pant at rest and reshape silently under movement.
functionality: Memory-fiber panels passively accommodate variable-geometry aug limbs through multiple configuration states without tearing or binding.
what_it_says: You have serious augmentation and the budget to dress around it properly.
worn_by: office workers with military-grade aug legs
mid-level corporate staff with aftermarket chrome
story_hooks: The memory-fiber panels retain a partial shape memory — a forensics tech can reconstruct what configuration a wearer's limb was in at a specific time.
Someone sold a counterfeit batch; the fake panels fail under rapid config cycling, seizing around the limb mid-transformation.
